stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite single-page app (runs in the browser, no server); GitHub REST API and the Claude API; node:test for the checking scripts; GitHub Pages deploy

idea.intent: A Product Owner turns a business need into an approved, measurable business intent in minutes.
idea.problem: Requests arrive as solutions or vague needs; without a measurable outcome nobody can tell whether the work succeeded.
idea.outcomeMetric: Every feature has an approved intent before requirements (baseline).
scopeIn: Ideation agent revises the need into an intent
Idea brief: problem, users, outcome metric, scope, risks
Approving the intent starts the Requirements agent

idea.intent: Requirements with testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria are drafted by an agent and approved by the PO/BA.
idea.problem: Hand-written requirements are slow and often not testable.
idea.outcomeMetric: Every requirement has acceptance criteria and an approval (baseline).
scopeIn: Approving the last draft starts the Design agent

features.name: Design: design tool and approval gate

idea.intent: No code is written before the PO/UX approve a design traced to the requirements.
idea.problem: Code built before anyone agreed on the screens has to be redone.
idea.outcomeMetric: Build is locked until the design is Approved (baseline).
scopeIn: Design agent drafts screens ↔ REQ ids

features.name: Test cases: one or more per requirement

idea.intent: Every requirement is covered by at least one test case before it is built.
idea.outcomeMetric: No requirement without a test case (baseline).

features.name: Build: coding agent, plan and pull request

idea.intent: Approved requirements become a reviewed pull request with a plan file, tests and passing guardrails.
idea.problem: AI-written code without guardrails, plan or review is risky to merge.
idea.outcomeMetric: Every agent PR carries a plan file and guardrail results (baseline).
scopeIn: Coding agent with RAG and tool calling

idea.intent: Several features are released together with one confirmed action.
idea.problem: Manual releases forget steps (CI check, tag, statuses).
idea.outcomeMetric: Releases are tagged and requirements marked Done (baseline).
scopeIn: Check CI, squash-merge, mark Done, tag, deploy

features.name: Compass Framework: install into repos safely

idea.intent: Any repo can be continued by any person or agent through the installed Compass Framework, without losing the repo's own files.
idea.problem: Without a shared contract, work depends on the portal or on one person.
idea.outcomeMetric: Install never overwrites a repo's own files (baseline).
scopeIn: compass/ spec, intent, design, plans, REVIEW.md

features.name: Compass follows its own delivery process

idea.need: make the compass repo itself follow the ai-native sdlc
idea.intent: From the next pull request on, 100% of Compass's own pull requests go intent → requirements → design → plan → checks and independent review (today: none are checked).
idea.problem: Compass enforces this process in other projects but not in its own code: no CI on pull requests, no tests, no plan and no review record.
idea.outcomeMetric: Share of Compass PRs checked by CI and independently reviewed: 0% → 100% from the first PR after setup.
scopeIn: No drift between compass/ and src/framework/
risks: The setup PR is larger than 12 files (the check starts after it)

features.name: Team floor: watch the agent team work, live

idea.need: recently, I see a few AI users they built a few creative team working with each other in a realtime movement user interface. Can we apply this for compass
idea.intent: From the Team floor alone, the Product Owner can tell within 5 seconds which agent is working, on which feature, and whether anything waits for her approval (today: only one run log at a time).
idea.problem: The pipeline is already a team with handoffs and approval gates, but the portal shows it as separate text logs, so who is working, who waits for whom and where a feature is stuck are hard to see.
idea.outcomeMetric: Time to answer "who is working, on what, and is anything waiting for me?": open each run (minutes) → one glance at the Team floor (≤ 5 seconds).
scopeIn: Team floor page with the 7 agents at desks
Live speech bubbles and activity list
Reduced motion, phone layout, demo mode
scopeOut: Several viewers on several devices (needs a server)
Sound, custom avatars, a game-like world
risks: A view only: drawn from the run trace already recorded; no change to agents, tools, guardrails or gates
No extra Claude calls or tokens, no paid service, no new libraries
Live means live in the browser tab that runs the agents

design.summary: A new "Team floor" page under the project in the sidebar. A floor shows the seven agents as characters at desks in pipeline order (Ideation → Requirements → Design → Test design on the top row; Coding → Review → Release back along the bottom row), joined by a corridor. A "Your approval" desk collects runs that wait for the Product Owner. Summary chips, a feature filter, Pause motion and a live activity list sit around the floor. Drawn in the honey design system (Bee There brand, rolled out to every page in F-010).

screens.name: Desktop · Live
screens.purpose: Normal day: one agent working, one waiting for approval, a handoff card moving.
elements: Summary chips (working / waiting / features in flight)
Your approval desk with Review & approve
states: Desk: Idle, Working, Waiting for you, Done, Rework
Approval waiting: honey desk + count in summary

screens.name: Desktop · Review sends work back
screens.purpose: A failed review moves the card back to the Coding agent along a coral path; nothing waits for approval.

screens.name: Phone · Live
screens.purpose: Same information on a phone: approval banner on top, desks in a 2-column grid in pipeline order, activity collapsed.

screens.name: Design notes
screens.purpose: Data source, desk states, motion timing, reduced motion, approval and filter behaviour.
elements: Motion: bubble updates ≤ 1 s, card glide ≈ 0.8 s
Reduced motion: no movement, card appears at the next desk

design.notes: Accessibility: desks are buttons with an accessible name ("Coding agent, working on F-008: Writing …"); state is never shown by colour alone (badge text); the activity list is an aria-live region (polite). Responsive: phone layout below 720 px.

features.name: Honey brand: Compass shares the Bee There look

idea.need: can you make a branding color and theme similar to 'bee there' with signature honey yellow — rebrand for all pages in compass
idea.intent: 100% of the portal's pages use the Bee There honey theme in light and dark mode, with no old teal colour left in the code (today: 0%, all teal).
idea.problem: Compass and Bee There look like unrelated products; the new Team floor design is already drawn in the honey brand.
idea.outcomeMetric: Pages on the honey theme: 0% → 100%; old teal colours in src/: many → 0 (checked by a test).
scopeIn: Shapes: pill buttons, rounded cards, warm shadows
scopeOut: A shared token package between the repos
risks: Change through the tokens in src/index.css, not page by page; no new libraries
Normal text keeps WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) in both modes
Nothing else changes: same pages, same behaviour

design.summary: Honey edition v0.2 of the Compass design system, taken from the Bee There tokens: honey #FFC629 brand with dark ink text on it, cream canvas, warm ink text, coral/mint/sky/violet accents; Lexend headings, Be Vietnam Pro body, JetBrains Mono for ids; radius 8/14/20/28 and pills; warm honey-tinted shadow. One meaning per colour: honey = brand and "your turn", sky = working/info, mint = done/success, coral = rework/error.

screens.name: Design system · Honey edition
screens.purpose: The single reference for colours (light and dark), type, shape, spacing, depth and components.
elements: Semantic colours in Light and Dark mode
Button, Badge, Agent desk, Handoff card

screens.name: Portal page in the honey theme (Team floor as example)
screens.purpose: Shows the theme applied to a full page: sidebar, nav, chips, buttons, cards.
elements: Sidebar with honey logo and selected nav

design.notes: Every other page keeps its layout and only takes the new tokens. Text colours are one shade darker than Bee There where needed (tertiary #6E6559, brand text #8A5F00, success #17704F, info #1B62B5, danger #B0432A; dark-mode tertiary #B3A999) so normal text reaches 4.5:1 on canvas, surface, subtle and honey-subtle backgrounds.

features.name: Readability follow-ups: status labels and phone stage strip

idea.need: turn the "Draft" vs "Approved" label colours and the cramped phone stage strip into requirements for later — yes please
idea.intent: The Product Owner tells Draft from Approved labels without reading them, and no word breaks in a feature's stage strip on a 390 px phone (today: both labels honey; words break mid-word).
idea.problem: After the honey rebrand, Draft (warning) and Approved (brand) labels are both honey; on phones the six stage cards of a feature page squeeze into narrow columns and break words.
idea.outcomeMetric: Draft vs Approved: same colour family → different families (test); broken words in the stage strip at 390 px: several → 0 (screenshot).
scopeIn: Status label colours on requirements, test cases and features
scopeOut: A redesign of the feature page
risks: Tokens of the honey design system only; no new libraries

design.summary: Two small changes inside the honey design system. Status labels: Draft uses the neutral tone (grey), Approved uses the success tone (mint, like Done), In build stays info (sky), on requirements, test cases and features. Phone stage strip: below 720 px the six stage cards of a feature page become a one-per-row list in stage order (stage chip, stage name, summary, agent · role, chevron); the current stage is highlighted honey. 720 px and wider stays as today.

screens.name: Status labels — before/after, light and dark
screens.purpose: Shows the new label colours and a requirements list using them.

screens.name: Phone · Feature stage strip as a list
screens.purpose: The stage strip of a feature page at 390 px: one stage per row, whole words.
elements: Stage name in its stage colour

design.notes: Desktop stage strip unchanged (TC-026). The desktop stage strip deliberately stays as it is (five columns; the sixth stage wraps), per the intent.

features.name: Delete a feature and close its GitHub issues

idea.need: Allow me to delete a feature directly from compass portal. The corresponding github ticket should also be deleted.
idea.intent: A feature added by mistake is gone from the portal, the spec and the repo in under 30 seconds, and its GitHub issues are closed as not planned (today: archive only; removing one means hand-editing spec.json and closing issues one by one).
idea.problem: A feature can only be archived. A mistaken or duplicate feature stays on the board and in spec.json for good, and its requirement issues stay open on GitHub.
idea.outcomeMetric: Time to remove a feature: hand-editing spec.json and closing each issue → one dialog under 30 s; open issues of a deleted feature: all → 0 (or a list of the ones GitHub refused).
scopeIn: Delete button and typed-id confirmation on the feature page
Removing the feature, its requirements, test cases, agent runs and generated files
Closing its open GitHub issues as not planned, with a comment
A strong warning when the feature has code
scopeOut: Removing code, tests, branches or pull requests of a built feature
An undo or trash bin (Archive stays the reversible option)
risks: Deletion cannot be undone in the portal: typing the feature id is the human approval
The token needs Issues: Read & write

design.summary: A "Delete feature" button sits next to "Archive feature" on the feature page and opens a centred dialog (full-width sheet on phones). The dialog lists what will be removed — requirements with their status, test cases, the three F-xxx.md files and the open GitHub issues that will be closed as not planned — and asks to type the feature id. Delete (red) is enabled only when the text is exactly the id. A built feature gets a red warning box above the list, naming the requirements In build or Done and its open pull requests, which stay open. After deleting, the feature board shows a notice: mint when every issue closed, honey with links when GitHub refused some.

screens.name: Desktop · Delete dialog, feature without code
screens.purpose: Everything that will be removed, and the typed-id confirmation, for a feature whose requirements are Draft or Approved.
elements: Title "Delete F-xxx · name?" and the Archive hint
"What will be removed": requirements with status badges, test cases, files, open issues
states: Esc or Cancel → closes, nothing changes

screens.name: Desktop · Delete dialog, feature with code
screens.purpose: The strong warning for a feature with requirements In build or Done and an open pull request.
elements: Red warning box naming the built requirements
Open pull requests with links, marked "stays open"
Hint "Delete stays off until the text is exactly F-xxx"
states: Text does not match → Delete disabled
No code and no open PR → no warning box (SCR-1)

screens.name: Phone · Dialog and result notice
screens.purpose: The dialog at 390 px with stacked buttons, and the notice on the feature board after deleting.
elements: Short summary of what will be removed
Full-width Delete feature and Cancel buttons
Honey notice listing issues GitHub refused, with link and reason
Mint notice when every issue was closed
states: Some issues still open (403: token needs Issues: Read & write)

design.notes: Keyboard: focus starts in the id field, Tab cycles inside the dialog, Esc cancels. The dialog scrolls inside itself on short screens. Text colours from the honey tokens only; the red Delete button uses text/danger with white text (contrast checked in build).

features.name: Team access: Google sign-in, project teams and roles

idea.need: Create a management module that allows admins to onboard users into projects and assign them specific roles. Each user can have multiple roles when needed. Users must log in with a Google account using the same email address registered in the system. This allows the system to identify which projects and roles they are authorized to access.
idea.intent: A BA, QA or designer can join a project in under 1 minute and can pass only the gates their roles own (today: anyone with the portal and a token can pass every gate, and nobody is identified).
idea.problem: Compass does not know who is using it. Whoever opens the portal on a device with a GitHub token can approve any gate, and approvals record "the Product Owner" instead of a real person.
users: Team members: PO, BA, UX, QA, Dev, DM, Ops
idea.outcomeMetric: Gates passable without the owning role: all → 0; time to onboard a team member: not possible → under 1 minute; approvals naming a real person: 0% → 100%.
scopeIn: Team page per project: add by email, several roles, change, remove
Sign in with Google matched by verified email
Role → gate rules in the portal and in Firestore security rules
A shared GitHub token per project, managed by its Admins
scopeOut: Moving ideas, runs or other project data to Firebase
risks: Any member can copy the shared GitHub token from the browser; removing a member does not revoke a copy (ADR-011)
New dependency: firebase (needs the human-approved label)
The Product Owner must create the Firebase project and publish the rules once
Free Spark plan limits (50k reads/day) — far above a small team

requirements.title: The Compass repo has the Compass Framework
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Compass repo to carry the same Compass Framework it installs into other projects, generated by the portal itself, so that any person or agent changing Compass follows the same process.
ac:
Given the Compass repository
When I open it
Then it has compass/ (spec.json, intent/, design/, plans/, REVIEW.md, guardrails.json and the checking scripts), AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the PR and issue templates and the Claude Code edit hook

Given the framework files in the repo
When they are compared with what the portal generates for this project
Then they were produced by the portal's own frameworkFiles(), not written by hand

requirements.title: Every pull request is checked by CI
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want every pull request to Compass checked automatically, so that a change without approvals, a plan or tests cannot be merged unnoticed.
ac:
Given a pull request to main
When CI runs
Then it runs the spec check, the guardrails check (main's copy, including the plan check), the unit tests and the build

Given a push to main
When the existing deploy workflow runs
Then the website deploy works exactly as before

requirements.title: The checking scripts have unit tests
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the checking scripts that Compass installs into every project to have their own tests, so that a broken check is caught before it reaches other projects.
ac:
Given the scripts in src/framework/
When npm test runs (Node's built-in runner, no new library)
Then it covers the spec check (traceability, intent, design gate), the plan check and the edit hook's decisions

Given a change that breaks one of these checks
When npm test runs
Then at least one test fails

requirements.title: The installed scripts never drift from the portal's copies
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the checking scripts in the repo's compass/ folder to stay identical to the copies the portal installs (src/framework/), so that Compass is checked by exactly the rules it gives other projects.
ac:
Given compass/check-spec.mjs, compass/check-guardrails.mjs, compass/guardrails-lib.mjs and compass/hooks/guard-edit.mjs
When one differs from its copy in src/framework/
Then npm test fails and names the file

requirements.title: Idea: business need revised into a business intent
requirements.story: As a product owner, I want to write a business need and get it revised into a measurable business intent, so that the work starts from an outcome.
ac:
Given a business need on the Idea page
When the Ideation agent runs and I approve its brief
Then the feature has the revised intent, my original need and a brief, and the Requirements agent starts

requirements.title: Requirements: generate and approve
requirements.story: As a business analyst, I want requirements drafted with Given/When/Then criteria, so that I only review and approve them.
ac:
Given an approved intent
When the Requirements agent runs and its proposal is accepted
Then Draft requirements appear; approving the last one starts the Design agent

requirements.title: Design: design tool, screens and approval gate
requirements.story: As a product owner, I want a design traced to the approved requirements and approved before coding, so that code is built to agreed screens.
ac:
Given a feature whose design is not Approved
When I open Build
Then coding is locked; after Approve design it is unlocked

requirements.title: Test cases: one or more per requirement
requirements.story: As QA, I want test cases generated for every uncovered requirement, so that nothing is built untested.
ac:
Given requirements without test cases
When the Test design agent runs and its proposal is accepted
Then each of them has a happy-path and a negative test case

requirements.title: Build: coding agent, plan file and pull request
requirements.story: As a developer, I want the coding agent to propose a change set that passes guardrails and opens a PR with a plan file, so that I only review the diff.
ac:
Given approved requirements and an approved design
When I approve the agent's change set
Then a branch and PR are opened with compass/plans/<REQ-ids>-<name>.md committed first

requirements.title: Release: merge, tag and deploy
requirements.story: As a delivery manager, I want to release several features in one confirmed step, so that releases are consistent.
ac:
Given approved agent PRs with green CI
When I confirm the release
Then they are merged, requirements are marked Done and a vX.Y.Z tag is created

requirements.title: Framework: install into repos without overwriting their own files
requirements.story: As a repo owner, I want Install framework to add only missing files, so that my repo's own scripts and docs are kept.
ac:
Given an existing repo with its own compass/*.mjs
When Install framework runs
Then only missing framework files are added, the generated spec views are refreshed and the repo's own files are listed as kept

requirements.title: The Team floor shows every agent at its desk with its current state
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want one page that shows all seven agents at their desks with their current state, so that I can see at a glance who is working, on which feature, and who waits for me.
ac:
Given a project with agent runs
When I open "Team floor" in the project sidebar
Then I see the seven agents at desks in pipeline order (Ideation, Requirements, Design, Test design, Coding, Review, Release), each with its name, the role it mirrors (Ideation PO, Requirements BA, Design UX, Test design QA, Coding Dev, Review QA, Release DM) and a state badge

Given an agent's latest run
When its status is running, awaiting-approval, approved/done, failed/rejected, or there is no open run
Then its desk shows Working, Waiting for you, Done, Rework or Idle, and the feature it works on

Given the summary above the floor
When runs change state
Then the counts of agents working, runs waiting for approval and features in flight update

Given the feature filter
When I choose one feature
Then only that feature's runs set the desks; desks without a run of that feature show Idle

requirements.title: What each agent is doing appears live in its speech bubble and the activity list
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see what each working agent is doing right now, so that I can follow the team without opening every run.
ac:
Given an agent with a running run
When a new step is recorded in its trace
Then within 1 second its speech bubble shows that step's title

Given the live activity list
When steps are recorded by any agent
Then the newest step appears at the top with its time, agent and title, and screen readers announce it politely

requirements.title: Handoffs move as cards between desks, and a failed review sends the card back
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see work moving from one agent to the next, so that I understand the flow and spot rework.
ac:
Given a run whose output passes to the next agent (for example approved requirements start the Design agent)
When the handoff happens
Then a card with the feature or REQ ids moves along the corridor from the first desk to the next one

Given the Review agent fails a change set
When the run goes back to the Coding agent
Then the card moves back along a coral path and the Coding desk shows Rework

requirements.title: Approvals can be given from the Team floor with the same result as from Agent runs
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to approve or reject waiting work straight from the Team floor, so that nothing waits on me longer than needed.
ac:
Given runs awaiting approval
When I look at the Your approval desk
Then it lists each waiting run (agent and feature) with a "Review & approve" button, and the desk says "Nothing waiting" when there is none

Given a waiting run
When I open it from the Team floor (approval desk or the agent's desk) and approve or reject it
Then the result is exactly the same as approving or rejecting it from Agent runs

requirements.title: The Team floor respects reduced motion, works on a phone and in demo mode, at no extra cost
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Team floor to be comfortable for everyone and free to run, so that I can use and demo it anywhere.
ac:
Given my device asks for reduced motion, or I press "Pause motion"
When the floor updates
Then nothing moves: desks, bubbles and lists still update and a handoff card simply appears at the next desk

Given a phone-sized screen (below 720 px)
When I open the Team floor
Then an approval banner is on top, the desks are in a 2-column grid in pipeline order and the activity list is collapsed

Given demo mode (no API key)
When agents run
Then the Team floor shows them the same way

Given the Team floor is open
When agents run
Then no extra Claude calls, tokens, network requests or libraries are used: everything comes from the run trace already recorded

requirements.title: Compass colours follow the honey design system in light and dark mode
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Compass to use the Bee There honey colours, so that both products look like one family.
ac:
Given the design tokens in src/index.css
When I compare them with the Figma page "🎨 Design system" (Honey edition v0.2)
Then the primitive and semantic colours match in light and dark mode, with honey #FFC629 as the brand colour and dark ink text on it

Given any state colour in the portal
When it is shown
Then honey means brand or "your turn", sky means working/info, mint means done/success and coral means rework/error

Given normal text on its background
When contrast is measured in light and dark mode
Then it is at least 4.5:1 (WCAG AA)

requirements.title: Compass type, shapes and logo follow the honey design system
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Compass to have the same friendly type and shapes as Bee There, so that the brand feels the same, not only the colours.
ac:
Given any heading
When it is shown
Then it uses Lexend SemiBold; body text stays Be Vietnam Pro and ids stay JetBrains Mono

Given buttons, chips, cards and the sidebar
When they are shown
Then buttons and chips are pills, cards use 20–28 px corners and the warm honey-tinted shadow

Given the logo in the sidebar, the mobile top bar and the browser tab
When it is shown
Then it is the honey square with the dark compass needle

requirements.title: No page keeps the old teal theme
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the rebrand to reach every page, so that no screen still looks like the old Compass.
ac:
Given every page of the portal (Projects, Agent architecture, Connections, Feature board, the feature stages, Release, Agent runs, Knowledge)
When I open it in light and dark mode
Then it uses the honey theme

Given the source code in src/
When the unit tests run
Then a test fails if any old teal colour (#EDFAF7, #D2F2EA, #6ECDB9, #38B09A, #0E7666, #0D5E52, #0C3A34) or a hard-coded colour outside the design tokens is found

requirements.title: Draft and Approved labels look different at a glance
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Draft and Approved labels of requirements and designs in different colours, so that I see at a glance what still needs my approval.
ac:
Given a requirement with status Draft (on the Requirements, Test cases, Feature or Build page) or a feature design with status Draft (Design page)
When its status label is shown
Then it uses the neutral (grey) tone

Given a requirement or a feature design with status Approved, on the same pages
When its status label is shown
Then it uses the success (mint) tone, like Done, in light and dark mode; In build stays info (sky)

Given the status labels (neutral, info and success tones)
When contrast is measured
Then their text keeps at least 4.5:1 on the label background in light and dark mode

requirements.title: The stage strip of a feature reads well on a phone
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the stage strip of a feature to stay readable on my phone, so that I can follow a feature anywhere.
ac:
Given a feature page on a screen narrower than 720 px
When the stage strip (Idea → Release) is shown
Then each stage takes the full width in one list, in stage order, and no word is broken across lines

Given a screen 720 px or wider
When the stage strip is shown
Then it looks as it does today

requirements.title: Delete a feature from its page after typing its id
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to delete a feature from its page, so that a feature added by mistake does not stay on the board for good.
ac:
Given a feature page
When I click "Delete feature" (next to "Archive feature")
Then a dialog lists what will be removed: the feature's requirements, test cases, files (compass/intent, features and design F-xxx.md) and its open GitHub issues

Given the delete dialog
When the text I type is not exactly the feature id (e.g. F-012)
Then the Delete button stays disabled

Given the delete dialog
When I press Esc or Cancel
Then the dialog closes and nothing is changed

Given I typed the feature id
When I click Delete
Then the feature is removed and I am back on the feature board, which no longer shows it

Given the dialog on a phone (390 px) or with the keyboard only
When I use it
Then it fits the screen, focus stays inside the dialog and every button can be reached with Tab

requirements.title: Deleting a feature removes everything that belongs to it
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want everything of a deleted feature removed from the spec and the repo, so that nothing is left behind and the checks stay green.
ac:
Given a feature is deleted
When the spec is updated
Then the feature, its requirements (featureId = the feature), its test cases and its agent runs are removed; a test case that also covers a requirement of another feature is kept without the deleted ids

Given a decision (ADR) references a deleted requirement
When the feature is deleted
Then the decision is kept and only the deleted ids are taken out of its reqIds

Given a project on GitHub
When the feature is deleted
Then one commit updates compass/spec.json and its views and deletes compass/intent, compass/features and compass/design F-xxx.md of that feature (only the ones that exist), and node compass/check-spec.mjs passes on the result

Given a demo project or a project without a repo
When the feature is deleted
Then it is removed locally and nothing is sent to GitHub

requirements.title: The deleted feature's open GitHub issues are closed as not planned
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the GitHub tickets of a deleted feature closed, so that the issue list does not show work that will never happen.
ac:
Given a feature is deleted in a project on GitHub
When its issues are looked up
Then every open issue (not pull request) whose title starts with one of the feature's REQ ids (e.g. "REQ-016: …" or "REQ-016, REQ-017: …") or names the feature id (e.g. "(F-012)") is selected, and no other issue

Given the selected issues
When the feature is deleted
Then each gets a comment that the feature was deleted in Compass on that date, and is closed with the reason "not planned"

Given GitHub refuses to close an issue (for example the token lacks Issues: Read & write)
When the feature is deleted
Then the feature is still deleted and the portal lists the issues that are still open, with links and the reason

Given the Connect page, or the error shown when GitHub refuses for lack of permission
When I read the token help
Then it asks for Issues: Read & write as well

requirements.title: A strong warning before deleting a feature that has code
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want a clear warning when a feature I am deleting is already built, so that I know its code and tests still need a clean-up.
ac:
Given a feature with a requirement In build or Done
When the delete dialog opens
Then a red warning names those requirements and says that code and tests in the repo still reference them and need a separate change

Given a feature with open agent pull requests
When the delete dialog opens
Then the pull requests are listed with links, and deleting the feature does not close or merge them

Given a feature whose requirements are all Draft or Approved and that has no open pull request
When the delete dialog opens
Then no warning is shown

requirements.title: An admin adds a person to a project by email with one or more roles
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to add a person to my project by email and give them one or more roles, so that they can work on the project in the roles they have.
ac:
Given I am an Admin of the project or the super admin
When I open the project's Team page
Then I see the team list (email, roles) and an "Add person" form with an email field and role checkboxes PO, BA, UX, QA, Dev, DM, Ops and Admin

When I enter "Ba@Example.com " and tick BA and QA and click Add
Then ba@example.com appears in the list with the roles BA and QA (email stored trimmed and in lower case)

Given the Add person form
When the email is not a valid address, no role is ticked, or the email is already on the team

Given I am signed in without the Admin role on this project and I am not the super admin

requirements.title: An admin changes a person's roles or removes them from the project
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to change someone's roles or remove them, so that access follows the person's current job.
ac:
Given a person on the team
When I change their role checkboxes and save
Then the list shows the new roles and their next action in the portal uses them

Given a person on the team
When I click Remove and confirm
Then they are gone from the list and, at their next page load, no longer see the project

Given the project has only one Admin
When anyone tries to remove that person or untick their Admin role
Then it is refused with "A project needs at least one Admin"

Given I remove a person
When the removal is saved
Then the page reminds me to replace the project's GitHub token, because they may have copied it

requirements.title: People sign in with Google and see only the projects whose team lists their email
requirements.story: As a team member, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that Compass knows which projects and roles are mine.
ac:
Given Firebase is configured and I am not signed in
When I open the portal
Then I see a "Sign in with Google" screen and no project data

Given I sign in with a Google account whose verified email matches a team entry (case-insensitive)
When sign-in completes
Then the Projects page shows only the projects whose team lists my email, and the header shows my email and Sign out

Given I sign in with a Google account that is on no team and is not the super admin
When sign-in completes
Then I see "You have no access yet — ask your admin" with my email and Sign out, and no project data

Given a Google account whose email is not verified
When it signs in
Then it is treated as having no access

Given Firebase is not configured (demo mode)
When I open the portal
Then it works as today without sign-in

requirements.title: Each approval gate can be passed only by a person with the role that owns it
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want each gate tied to its role, so that only the right person can approve each stage.
ac:
Given the gate rules: intent and requirements → PO (BA may also approve requirements); design → UX or PO; test cases → QA; start a build → Dev; merge and release → DM or PO; team and token → Admin
When a signed-in person opens a gate whose role they do not have
Then its button is disabled with the hint "Needs the <role> role"

Given a person with several roles (e.g. BA and QA)
When they open the requirements and test-case gates
Then both are enabled, and the design and release gates are disabled

Given a person changes the page in the browser to enable a disabled gate
When the approval is saved
Then the Firestore security rules refuse it and the portal shows "Not allowed for your roles"

Given the super admin
When they open any gate
Then it is enabled

requirements.title: A project Admin stores one GitHub token that the project's members use
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to save one GitHub token for the project, so that members without their own GitHub account can save their work to the repo.
ac:
Given I am an Admin of the project

Then I can paste a token, test it and save it; the help asks for a fine-grained token for this repo only, with Contents, Pull requests and Issues: Read & write and an expiry date

Given a saved project token and a signed-in member without their own token

Given a member who is not an Admin

Given the token is missing, expired or refused by GitHub

requirements.title: The super admin sees every project and can make someone a project Admin

Given the super admin email is set once in the Firebase settings (the Product Owner's Google account)

decisions.title: Compass follows its own delivery process
decisions.context: Compass enforced the AI-native SDLC in other repos but not on its own code.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner approved the intent: Compass's own repo gets the Compass Framework generated by the portal itself, CI on every pull request, tests for the checking scripts and a no-drift check between compass/ and src/framework/.
decisions.consequences: Every later Compass PR needs an approved intent, approved requirements, a design (or none: <reason>), a plan file and an independent review. The setup PR is larger than 12 files because the check does not exist on main yet.

decisions.title: Light baseline for the existing portal
decisions.context: The portal existed before its repo had a spec.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose a light baseline: one feature per stage (F-001…F-007) with one Done requirement each (REQ-101…107); detailed requirements are written only for new work.
decisions.consequences: Older behaviour is documented at stage level only; new work starts at REQ-001.

decisions.title: Team floor is a live view of the existing run trace
decisions.context: The Product Owner asked for a realtime "creative team" interface like those other AI users built.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner approved the intent for option 1: a Team floor page drawn only from the run trace Compass already records. Agents talking to each other and multi-device viewing are out of scope, each needing its own decision.
decisions.consequences: No change to agents, tools, guardrails or approval gates; no extra Claude cost; live only in the browser tab that runs the agents.

decisions.title: Compass shares the Bee There honey brand on every page
decisions.context: The Team floor design was drawn in a new Figma file; the Product Owner asked for the Bee There look with its signature honey yellow.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose to rebrand all Compass pages (not only the Team floor) to the Honey edition of the design system in the Figma file "Compass — Team floor", which becomes the project design tool. Honey means brand and "your turn"; working moves from amber/teal to sky so the two never look alike.
decisions.consequences: The teal theme is retired; the colour tokens in src/index.css follow the Figma variables; a test keeps old teal out of src/. Where Bee There's text colours fall below WCAG AA 4.5:1 (grey #8A8072, brand text #A87400, and the state texts on pale honey), Compass uses one shade darker; the Product Owner approved this on 2026-11-26.

decisions.title: Team access uses Firebase on the free Spark plan
decisions.context: Compass is a browser-only app without a server. Team lists and role checks must be shared between people and cannot be trusted if they live only in each browser.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose Firebase Auth (Google sign-in) and Firestore on the free Spark plan, with Firestore security rules as the real gate, over a team.json file in each repo or browser-only storage.
decisions.consequences: New dependency firebase and a firestore rules file (both need the human-approved label); the Product Owner creates the Firebase project and publishes the rules once; ideas, runs and other data stay where they are.

decisions.title: Members use a shared GitHub token per project
decisions.context: GitHub writes need a token. Team members who sign in with Google may have no GitHub account or token.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose one GitHub token per project, stored by its Admins and readable by its members, over each member connecting their own token.
decisions.consequences: Every member's browser holds the token, so a member could copy it and removing them does not revoke that copy. Mitigation: the portal asks for a fine-grained token for that repo only (Contents, Pull requests, Issues) with an expiry date, and reminds Admins to replace it after removing someone.
